title: HFCL Q2 FY27 Profit Soars 448%; Revenue Up 143% YoY
text:

 TECHNOLOGY Author Kavya Nair | Published at: 26th October 2026, 8:05 pm Add as a Preferred Source on Google HFCL Limited delivered its strongest quarterly performance ever, with net profit surging 448% to Rs 394.22 crore and revenue jumping 143% to Rs 2,541.79 crore. The company raised its annual revenue growth guidance to 80% and reported a massive order book of Rs 28,900 crore. While the EPC division reported temporary losses, management expects a swift recovery as the firm aggressively expands into defence, aerospace, and high-capacity optical manufacturing.
 HFCL Delivers Record-Breaking Q2 Performance
 Revenue grew 143.62% YoY to Rs 2,541.79 crore; Net profit jumped 448.14% to Rs 394.22 crore.
 Reader Takeaway: Robust export demand and order book strength drive results, though investors should monitor temporary EPC segment losses.
 What just happened
 HFCL reported its best-ever quarterly performance for Q2 FY27, marked by significant margin expansion of 640 basis points to 25.89%. The company’s explosive growth was fueled by a 493% YoY surge in export revenues. Management has demonstrated significant confidence by doubling its annual revenue growth guidance from 40% to 80%.
 Why this matters
 The company’s order book now stands at an impressive Rs 28,900 crore, providing long-term revenue visibility. The shift toward higher-margin products and backward integration in optical fiber manufacturing is effectively driving profitability. Additionally, the strategic move into the defence and aerospace sector, supported by a planned Rs 1,600 crore order book acquisition, signals a new revenue pillar for the company.
 Strategic Growth Drivers
 HFCL is committing Rs 1,800 crore in capital expenditure to scale its optical fiber and cable manufacturing. A key highlight is the decision to double preform capacity to 600 MT, which will lower production costs. The defence vertical is targeted to contribute Rs 500 crore in FY27, with long-term goals of reaching Rs 5,000 crore within three years.
 Risks to watch
 The EPC segment posted losses this quarter due to timing mismatches in milestone billing. While management projects a return to profitability by Q1 of the next fiscal year, investors should track this closely. Other risks include minor delays in receiving machinery for capacity expansion and exposure to broader geopolitical volatility impacting global data center demand.
 What to track next
 Watch for the successful integration of the aerospace acquisition and the commissioning of new preform manufacturing facilities. The conversion rate of the Rs 28,900 crore order book into actual billings will remain the primary metric for sustained stock performance.
